section: 12. Dragon-Slaying Weapon Forging: Silver Ingot into the Furnace
description: Melt the silver ingot in the military camp's iron furnace, roll 8d6 to forge silver weapons effective against dragons. The bard jests about the cost of all this trouble.

conversation.text: .player6's dagger cuts a cold silver arc in the dim tomb chamber. "Crack!" The blade precisely strikes the rusted iron chain link. The decayed metal snaps like a dry branch. The chain instantly shatters, links breaking apart and clattering to the ground, raising a cloud of ancient dust.

conversation.speaker: player6

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Everyone pushes the wooden door open, and blinding sunlight instantly pours down. The ruins of the Church of Saint Mokios stand silent under the afternoon sun. Half of the church's dome has collapsed, broken stone pillars lie slanted in the rubble like ribs snapped by a giant. Charred beams span above the altar, still emitting wisps of smoke. The adjacent building is completely reduced to ruins, with only a solitary wall standing abruptly, a half-burned icon still clinging to its surface. Ten statues of the Virgin Mary are scattered in the church courtyard. The white marble of the eight small statues is grayed by smoke but intact. One of the two giant statues is broken at the waist, while the other still stands among the ruins, its gilded robe hem reflecting glaring light. A large relief spreads at the base of a wall: Saint George's steed rears high, its spear piercing the throat of a monster with a long neck, short wings, and a dog-headed, dragon-bodied form. The wave patterns under the monster's claws suggest it rose from a great lake or sea.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: #Give a bitter smile.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: In the distance, the sound of splashing water comes from the direction of the reservoir.

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: #Stroke my singed beard. "Why do you think they moved the guns away back then?"

conversation.speaker: player9
conversation.text: "I must report the situation to Count Baldwin. This place is..." #Look at the church ruins.

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "The Seventh Hill... San Moqius Church..."

conversation.speaker: player9
conversation.text: "What are you going there for?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "In a secret compartment at the base of an ivory Madonna statue holding the Holy Infant, there is a scroll hidden by the old priest, recording how to track the 'Devil's Simulacrum'."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "It seems that's the place." #Points at the burned-down cathedral. "There might still be evildoers guarding it."

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "I think we still need to observe vigilantly."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "This is something a group of cultists calling themselves 'Unfettered Flesh' are looking for."

conversation.speaker: player8
conversation.text: "That's the situation."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "The Count also sent us to investigate these 'Unfettered Flesh' people. We need to kill one or two and then go to the old docks to find a leper to report back."

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "Surveillance may not be everywhere, but it remembers faces."

conversation.speaker: player9
conversation.text: "To be honest, we all came here because that blind Venetian Doge tricked us. He couldn't pay, and now look at us—a bunch of mercenaries. Is it worth risking our lives for them?"

conversation.speaker: player7
conversation.text: "At least the Count is really rich."

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: "So, you mean we should go back to the Count first and explain the situation?"

conversation.speaker: player9
conversation.text: "You just said a Madonna statue holding the Holy Infant, right... Let me see." #Looking at the statues among the church ruins to see if any match.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: player6 glanced at the Virgin Mary statue that player7 couldn't move and silently stepped forward. She first walked around to the side of the statue, running her fingertips along the seam between the base and the ground, scraping off a layer of old grime. Then, she took half a step back and suddenly delivered a side kick, heavily striking the side of the statue's base. Half a second later, the statue tilted and she pushed it over, crashing onto the nearby pile of ruins and breaking into two pieces. The severed head of the Virgin Mary rolled a few times and stopped at player7's feet, its expression still sorrowful. Yet, there was still no hidden compartment in the base.

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: The heavy church doors were suddenly pushed open. In the blinding sunlight, a tall, thin figure draped in tattered monk's robes stood silhouetted against the light. The metal eyepatch on his face gleamed coldly, while his one good eye swept over the interior of the church like a snake, his gaze shifting between the toppled Virgin Mary statue and the disheveled investigators. "Ah... lost lambs. How did you get in?"

conversation.speaker: player6
conversation.text: [Swatting cockroaches]

conversation.speaker: player3
conversation.text: Suddenly, the impostors simultaneously drew crossbows from behind their backs. The sound of crossbow mechanisms echoed sharply through the church as over a dozen iron bolts shot from different angles toward the area where the four were. Amid the whistling of arrows tearing through the air, the cultists disguised as soldiers and monks behind the rubble piles maintained mechanical precision in their reloading movements. The distribution of the first volley of arrows embedded in the ground revealed tactical coordination: one-third blocked the route to the courtyard, two formed an angle to cut off retreat along the western wall with reliefs, and the densest concentration was focused around the toppled Virgin Mary statue—the investigators' location. Two cultists disguised as monks were flanking along the ruined pillars of the side aisle, holding kukri knives.
